title: NestJS Examples
description: Each example belongs to one starter lesson. Follow its setup steps before trying it. These examples need the named tools and do not run in this site playground.

examples.title: Make a controller route
examples.description: A controller holds request handlers. @Get maps GET /hello to its method.

examples.title: Return named data
examples.description: Nest sends returned objects as JSON. Open GET /book.

examples.title: Read a route parameter
examples.description: @Param reads a named part of the route. Open GET /hello/Ravi.

examples.title: Read a query value
examples.description: @Query reads the query string. Visit GET /search?q=cat.

examples.title: Check and parse a number
examples.description: ParseIntPipe reads an integer or rejects bad input. GET /double/4 uses the checked number.

examples.title: Read a request body
examples.description: @Body supplies parsed JSON. Send POST /books with application/json and {"title":"Moon Trip"}.

examples.title: Share a service
examples.description: A provider is a shared helper supplied by Nest. The controller asks for Books in its constructor. Open GET /book.

examples.title: Supply a default query
examples.description: DefaultValuePipe supplies a value before ParseIntPipe checks it. Open GET /page with no query.

examples.title: Choose a reply status
examples.description: @HttpCode changes a handler status. POST /check returns 200 instead of the usual Nest POST status.

examples.title: Add a response header
examples.description: @Header adds metadata to a response. Open GET /note and inspect its Cache-Control header.

examples.title: Send a client to another route
examples.description: @Redirect sends a location to the client. A browser following GET /start ends at /hello.

examples.title: Report a missing item
examples.description: A built-in exception creates an HTTP error response. GET /missing reports a missing book.
